name: Murugan Idli Shop
signature_dish: Soft steamed idli served with four chutneys, sambar and milagai podi
why_it_matters: Founder S Manoharan's parents ran Murugan Coffee Nilayam in Madurai over 50 years ago; his mother's idlis became so popular a whole day's batch sold out in half an hour. Manoharan opened the first Murugan Idli Shop in Madurai in 1991 and brought it to Chennai's G N Chetty Road, T Nagar, in 2003. Outlets steam 10,000-12,000 idlis daily — the four-chutney plate is the reference Madras idli experience.
insider_tip: Order the idli with all four chutneys plus ghee podi idli — most visitors only take sambar. Madurai-origin jigarthanda is the under-ordered finisher. Heaviest queues 8-10am breakfast; turnover is fast so the wait moves. Cash + UPI.
signature_address: G N Chetty Road, T Nagar, Chennai, Tamil Nadu 600017

name: Mylai Karpagambal Mess
signature_dish: Keerai vadai — large spinach-batter vadai, with rava pongal and aviyal
why_it_matters: Founded 1953 by Ramadas Iyer under a thatched roof on East Mada Street facing the Kapaleeshwarar temple tank — one of the oldest surviving eating houses in Mylapore, now run by the third generation. A no-frills brahmin mess serving variety-yet-homely tiffin in the heart of old Madras; the keerai vadai and rava-pongal-with-aviyal combination are its signatures.
insider_tip: Sit before the temple-darshan crowd hits — go by 8.30am for breakfast or before 1pm for the meals. The keerai vadai is the dish to order that you won't find elsewhere. Right on the Mada Street loop around Kapaleeshwarar, so easy to fold into a temple visit. Cash preferred.
signature_address: 20 East Mada Street, Mylapore, Chennai, Tamil Nadu 600004

name: Ratna Cafe
signature_dish: Sambar idli — idli drowned in the cafe's signature sambar poured from mini buckets
why_it_matters: Founded 1948 by Jaggilal Gupta, a migrant from Mathura, Uttar Pradesh — Ratna Cafe rose to fame on its sambar, carried around in mini buckets and poured over idli and dosa. It makes 1,500-2,000 litres of sambar a day and popularised basundi, rasmalai and rose/badam milk in Chennai. Now run by the fourth generation of the Gupta family.
insider_tip: Order sambar idli and ask for an extra round of sambar — the staff pour it freely, and that is the whole point of the place. The basundi and rasmalai are the north-Indian sweets that made the cafe's reputation. Breakfast is busiest; mid-morning is calmer. Cash + UPI.
signature_address: 255 Triplicane High Road, Triplicane, Chennai, Tamil Nadu 600005

name: Buhari Hotel
signature_dish: Chicken 65 — the spicy deep-fried chicken starter the hotel invented in 1965
why_it_matters: Opened 1951 on Mount Road by A M Buhari, a former Sheriff of Madras — the first stand-alone fine-dining restaurant in post-independence Madras. Chicken 65 was invented here in 1965; the year-named follow-ups (Chicken 78, 82, 90) confirm the naming logic. The Mount Road branch still stands at its original site.
insider_tip: Order the original Chicken 65 — this is its birthplace — and pair with mutton biryani. The year-coded chicken dishes (78, 82, 90) are progressively different spice profiles, not just menu padding. Anna Salai branch is the heritage one; multiple newer outlets exist. Cash + cards.
signature_address: 83 Anna Salai, Mount Road, Chennai, Tamil Nadu 600002

name: Ponnusamy Hotel
signature_dish: Chettinad-style crab masala with fish fry and parotta
why_it_matters: Started in 1954 as a small mess in Royapettah by A R Velupillai of Ramanathapuram district — over 70 years it became a Chettinad non-veg landmark serving cinema stars and politicians. Tamil Nadu Tourism named it Best Non-Vegetarian Restaurant 2018-19. Masalas are ground fresh daily; the crab masala and shark/anchovy fries are dishes most Chennai restaurants skip.
insider_tip: Order crab masala plus a fish fry with parotta, and try sooraputu (shark) if available — these are the Chettinad-coast dishes that built the name. Weekend evenings get a steady crowd; call ahead. The Royapettah branch is the original. Cash + cards.
signature_address: Royapettah, near Royapettah Police Station, Chennai, Tamil Nadu 600014

name: Hotel Saravana Bhavan
signature_dish: South Indian meals and tiffin — masala dosa, mini tiffin, filter coffee
why_it_matters: Saravana Bhavan was founded in 1981 by P Rajagopal, who started with a KK Nagar grocery store and built India's best-known pure-vegetarian chain, now in dozens of countries. The Usman Road, T Nagar outlet is one of the long-running flagship Chennai branches, opposite the Shiva Vishnu temple — the default reliable South Indian meal for first-time visitors.
insider_tip: Order the mini tiffin to sample idli, vada, pongal and dosa in one platter, finished with the strong filter coffee. Cleanliness and consistency are the draw — a safe first meal on arrival. Usman Road branch is in the thick of T Nagar shopping; expect crowds at lunch. Cash + cards + UPI.
signature_address: 77 Usman Road, T Nagar, Chennai, Tamil Nadu 600017

name: Dindigul Thalappakatti Restaurant
signature_dish: Dindigul-style biryani — seeraga samba rice with a secret spice blend
why_it_matters: Thalappakatti began in Dindigul in 1957 and has served its short-grain seeraga-samba biryani for over six decades, expanding to Chennai and beyond. The Dindigul style — smaller rice, distinct spice mix, separate from the Ambur and Hyderabadi schools — is best sampled here; locals consistently rank it among Chennai's top biryani addresses.
insider_tip: Order mutton biryani for the seeraga samba rice that defines Dindigul style — it eats lighter than Hyderabadi. Pair with chicken chukka. Multiple Chennai branches; Nungambakkam and Anna Nagar are the central ones. Cash + cards + UPI.
signature_address: Nungambakkam High Road, Nungambakkam, Chennai, Tamil Nadu 600034

name: Sangeetha Veg Restaurant
signature_dish: Mini tiffin platter — idli, vada, pongal, mini dosa with filter coffee
why_it_matters: A widely-loved Chennai pure-veg chain known for its canteen-style mini tiffin and reliable South and North Indian fare at value prices. The Gandhi Irwin Road, Nungambakkam outlet near Egmore station is a dependable tiffin-and-filter-coffee stop, popular with families and travellers needing a quick clean meal.
insider_tip: The mini tiffin is the order — a sampler of South Indian classics on one platter. Goes well as a budget alternative to Saravana Bhavan. Gets crowded at peak meal hours with a short wait. Cash + cards + UPI.
signature_address: 23 Gandhi Irwin Road, Nungambakkam, Chennai, Tamil Nadu 600008

name: Mathsya Restaurant
signature_dish: Pre-set South Indian tiffin combo — idli, vada, pongal, masala dosa with filter coffee
why_it_matters: A long-running vegetarian dining address in T Nagar known for its buffet South Indian breakfast and pre-set tiffin combos — idli, vada, pongal, masala dosa and poori served together and finished with strong filter coffee. A comfortable, slightly upmarket alternative to the canteen-style messes in the same neighbourhood.
insider_tip: Come for the buffet breakfast to sample the full spread of South Indian tiffin in one sitting. The combo plate is the efficient à la carte option. Calmer and more spacious than the busy Usman Road tiffin joints nearby. Cash + cards.
signature_address: 1 Venkatanarayana Road, T Nagar, Chennai, Tamil Nadu 600017
